item.title: Re: Greenlight - To Go Hell and Back
item.content:encoded:
Asked to take a look at this, apologies for the delay.

So like, the general shape of what you have here is good. It's a very emotional narrative, clear beginning and end, etc. But like, you're pulling a lot of elements into this, and it becomes a tad unfocused. Like, the Gate Guardian and 343 are extremely old and generally not looked upon fondly by modern audiences, as is your portrayal of the Serpent's Hand as a sort of… murderous, militarized force. You're also pulling stuff in from Three Moons — it's extremely all over the place in site lore, and I'd recommend you focus on one particular thing to make it work.

Question, err, how did O5-2 and Orpheus meet (and why do they have the names of greek characters)? Additionally, how did O5-2 let her guard slip enough to get killed? How did the information leak? Etc.

item.title: Re: Explaining My Plot Holes
item.content:encoded:
Collapsed for scrolling convenience.

+ show block
– hide block

I think I’ve pinned down my main concern with your idea thus far. Let’s talk about the classic movie The Lion King.

The story of The Lion King is undeniably derived from Hamlet; elements are missing, but the core narrative is there. And yet, the characters and plot beats have been tweaked to fit both the animalistic setting and the young target audience. Duplicitousness agents became lazy meercat/warthog combos, aurally-administered poison became a herd of wildebeest, and a rather tragic ending became heroic.

To put it another way, The Lion King succeeds as an adaptation because every aspect of it is altered to fit its new setting. If its characters remained the same as in the original text, it would feel disjointed at best and nonsensical at worst.

That is, I’m afraid, how I see your current idea pitch. The characters of Eurydice and Orpheus are not adapted to suit the setting of the SCP universe. By drawing them verbatim from the original story and dropping them into the canon untouched, there’s a disconnect between the events and the characters here that drags the whole concept down.


If you respond to this comment and would like me to see it, please send me a Wikidot PM, as I will not be notified otherwise.

item.title: Re: Greenlight - To Go Hell and Back
item.content:encoded:
Follow up, per author request:

+ show block
– hide block

After O5-2 doesn’t report to several meetings, the O5 Council begins an investigation. They find O5-2 easily, as an anomalous event in Oregon is investigated, finding a deceased female matching the description of O5-2. Her body is taken in, with no evidence as to why she was there or how she died.

How could this be allowed to happen? The O5 council being as important as they are, having on just up and vanish seems like it would set off a lot of red alerts before getting to this point.

While Eurydice is paranoid for obvious reasons, she lets her guard down with Orpheus, thinking he will protect her.

Protect her more than all the MTF and security officers the Foundation has at their disposal? There is letting your guard down, and there is just asking for trouble. This seems like the latter.

In melancholy, he attempts to resurrect his love. He asks SCP-343 “how to resurrect Eurydice,” in which SCP-343 tells him that “it requires Orpheus to convince the Arch-Drudgeon,” something SCP-343 doesn’t want to get involved with. Orpheus establishes a plan and first enters The Wanderer’s Library to find “The Song of Minor,” fighting several SH members and subduing an entity known as Cerberus to obtain the lyrics to the song.

How does he get to SCP-343? If this dude is an SH member, how is he getting to an SCP the Foundation has in custody? It's not like he can just waltz in the front door of Site-19.

He arrives to Site 0 and uses a verse to please SCP-001, with the anomaly leading Orpheus through the gate and directly to JALAKARA’s doorstep.

While I'm pretty sure you mean the Gate Guardian, please keep in mind we have so, so many SCP-001s. You need to be more specific.

While the focus here is a lot more narrow than the previous version of the idea you offered, it does still feel quite clustered for what essentially boils down to a retelling of a fairly well known Greek myth.

Even if you narrow the scope down further, I'm not too sure how the reception for such a close 1:1 transfer of a well-known story into the SCP mythos would be.

I think you still need more refinement on this idea, and repair of the current plot holes as mentioned above before I would be fine offering the greenlight.

Best of luck.

item.title: Explaining My Plot Holes
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your critique.

[+] Open for Response
[-] Explaining my Plot Holes

I understand where you’re coming from with my cross-references being mostly from Series I, but I haven’t found any other SCPs to fill the role of Zeus (SCP-343), Hermes (SCP-001 leading Orpheus), or an entrance into the underworld (the Gate at Site 0). I feel like JALAKARA is a good pick for Hades and Eurydice being an O5 member would be a good reason as to why the Foundation is even involved.

In terms of the Abrahamic Figures, I do have a distaste for using these SCPs instead of Greek anomalies, but I think introducing the Greek Figures without a defined SCP would make the file too cluttered with unlisted anomalies. I personally don’t find it satisfying to reference an entity without having an already made file of the anomaly. But something that can be explained as in the custody of another GoI (like Cerberus) is accepted. But these Greek Gods would most likely be in the custody of the Foundation or at least beyond the Foundation’s control (JALAKARA).

In terms of the Serpent’s Hand, they do serve two purposes to the story (something I couldn’t explain due to the word limit). 1) They obviously want to take down the Foundation, and a distracted O5 member would make easy prey; 2) they are now tying up the loose end of Orpheus, as he is the only person able to resurrect Eurydice. Orpheus had the goal to resurrect her, and once he failed all he knew was that she was dead. To be with her, it meant he had to die.

I feel like the thread is missing the aspect of Orpheus’ motivation: to simply resurrect Eurydice.
He has no reason to destroy the Serpent’s Hand or ask the Foundation for help, he simply wants Eurydice back. Once he fails his trial and looks back, he has the need to kill himself to see her in the afterlife. That was the goal for Orpheus and his death, but of course I couldn’t explain this due to the word limit.


I hope this explains the plot holes you have noted and I hope you find this post informative on the story. If you want me to still flush out certain aspects, I am willing to do so, but I feel like this post is the one that explains the plot holes.

Again, thank you for the critique.

item.title: Re: Greenlight - To Go Hell and Back
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

After finding the body of O5-2 and SH members, they quickly let the Foundation take over.

The identity of the O5 council is kept secret; how do the UIU know it's O5-2?

The UIU’s investigation is the only evidence found until SCP-343’s cell is breached, with cameras showing a “shadow” talking to SCP-343 and discussing “how to resurrect immortals.” The Foundation starts retracing O5-2’s steps to see what led up to her death. Before piecing it together, Site 0 sounds the alarms of a breach and sees SCP-001 taking 3 steps away from the gate. A battle ensues between Orpheus and the SH before the Gate Guardian vaporizes the 1km region.

I'm going to be extremely honest here: this section is too summarised. I don't know how we get from 'shadow talking to 343' to 'foundation linking this to O5-2's steps' to '001 steps away from the gate' to 'battle ensues' at all.

While the initial plan of killing her was executed, Orpheus deduced that they were SH members.

Surely this should be 'Orpheus deduce that they tricked him' and like…how did he figure that out?

SCP-343 tells him that it requires “the convincing of The Guardian and the pleasing of the Spider God.”

Why does it need the guardian and jalakara? This feels like it's kinda real convoluted for no real reason other than to involve more groups of interest?

JALAKARA requests the TMI to allow the souls of both Orpheus and Eurydice to leave Corbenic once a year and explore Earth, with the Foundation agreeing to the terms.

how does JALAKARA have both the souls? did Orpheus not succeed in reviving Eurydice?

I think my central concern with this is that, it feels like this is an incredibly complex story but it also doesn't feel interesting? It still has a tonne of moving parts and stuff; but at the end of the day, it's a very detached-ly told love story and I can't help but feel like this would be a lot better as a tale from Orpheus's perspective still.

item.title: Re: Greenlight - To Go Hell and Back
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

After hundreds of people arrive in Corbenic, the Three Moons Initiative begin a joint operation with the Foundation to find out what is happening.

Can the TMI not just ask the people who arrived in Corbenic what happened?

They join the UIU as they survey the damage of Three Portlands and find the bodies of O5 members in anomalously destroyed sites.

I'm confused, is this implying that the SCPF has sites in Three Portlands? Obviously "no canons" applies, but that goes super counter to a huge amount of the established lore of 3Ports, namely the Foundation is super not welcome there. If not, then how did the Foundation not notice ENTIRE SITES being destroyed sooner?

They see a battle take place before the Gate Guardian crashes down and stops the battle.

The hell is the Gate Guardian doing there? Its been a while, but last I checked the Gate Guardian is very much guarding a single location.

The SH begins a civil rights movement for reality benders in Three Portlands

"No canons" rules applying again, but 3Ports is generally viewed as the kind of place where reality benders would already be viewed as people. That kind of civil rights movement wouldn't really be needed there. At all.

Three Portlands undergoes a civil war as Activist fight against Foundation sympathizers, who believe that reality benders are too powerful to be treated normally.

Foundation sympathizers would generally be in such a low minority in Three Portlands that this would be a very small and heavily one-sided conflict.

This war causes hundreds of people to arrive at Corbenic.

Why would this stand out compared to any other reason people die and arrive on Corbenic for any other mundane reason on a given day?

The SH and CI realize that to win this war, they must destroy the Foundation.

Last I checked, both the SH and the CI kind of have the destruction of the Foundation as an end goal as a default. This really doesn't seem like a thing they would just now, after starting a civil war, would realize.

The SH, CI, and GOC begin hunting the O5 Council, killing Eurydice first and injuring Orpheus (a reality bender with his anomalous harp).

How do they know where the O5 council is?

convincing the O5 Council (besides O5-1 because he was assigned to the investigation) to help him.

Why would the O5 members, with the ENTIRE SCP FOUNDATION at their disposal try to go this mission themselves instead of delegating it to what I'm sure are a multitude of much, much better trained MTFs?

All in all, my overall impression is that you throw a lot of GoIs into this, but don't really quite use them effectively, and often come across as if you only have a cursory understanding of what it is that makes reading about each of them fun to explore. I'd argue parring this down to just focus on the SH would likely be most in tune for what you are going for, since it would seem to me that CI and GOC involvement just adds bloat and doesn't really add that much to the story.

A retelling of the Orpheus myth in the SCP Foundation universe certainly could fly with the correct execution. But as of the time of writing, I don't think this would be it.

Best of luck.

item.title: The Major Changes
item.content:encoded:
This post is for reference of possible changes
No need to look here

So I made a bunch of changes that differs from my original concept. Here is a list of the changes I have made.

  • It was noted that the 6 anomalous groups make the story muddy, especially that the main focus is suppose to be Orpheus and Eurydice. So I decided to divide the whole thing into two different stories. This is described above in the page layout.
  • The goals of the Serpent’s Hand, GOC, and the Chaos Insurgency are different but I felt that if they all agreed on a common consensus they were willing to work with each other. This is described above.
  • The story of Orpheus was muddied, but I wanted him to fight the 3 groups with help of the Foundation, so I decided to reference the original actions of Orpheus from the myth as a way to tie in the idea that the myth occurs. I explain above the several events that are easily understood.
  • So I tried to tie in personal motivation to a rights issue, as the group appeared to have used the backdrop of the protest to punctuate the personal gain (that’s even confusing to explain), so I made it all centered around the protesting of civil rights rather than a duo of personal and social motivation.
  • Admittedly, the joint operation get too involved with the actions of Orpheus, kind of influencing him rather than him thinking of how to save Eurydice. I changed this to make Orpheus use the O5 council to help him. He’s the puppet master of the actions.

All in all, I tried to divide the actions of the anomalous groups into one story. The second story is the story of Orpheus, with the anomalous groups as reference.

item.title: Re: Greenlight - To Go Hell and Back
item.content:encoded:
Only look if you’re -ebonbonb-
- List of Things for Editing the Thread

Yes you are right with the cohesiveness and the several plot holes on my article. A few things I need to point out.

I should have listed this above in that a majority of the addendums are retrieved files, emails, or audio logs from personnel of the GoIs. It’s kind of like all these events are occurring and happening so fast that the Foundation is essentially playing catch up by surveying the damage.

This article is more of a collection of different files, logs, and emails with the Foundation piecing the whole story. A reference is SCP-5555, where a series of video logs, emails, and notes tell the story.

I feel like the important thing is that this article is the first instance of the SCP Foundation and the major Groups of Interest finally giving basic civil rights to reality benders, treating them as people rather than as an anomalous item.
Now that I got that out of the way, I feel like I can respond to the discrepancies that you gave1.

  1. Yes, the anomalous event does involve the harp. It’s a fight between the bad GoIs and Orpheus.
  2. Again, I should have broken this down more effectively. When I mean by civilian casualties, the civilians are of Three Portlands. The anomalous event explained on #1 is the first event that occurs outside of Three Portlands, while all the death is occurring in Three Portlands. This is kind of why the Foundation, TMI, and the UIU are barely finding out. This war is involving the battle for civil rights that I later described. The narrative is that Orpheus was once a part of the civil rights movement, but gave it up for Eurydice. It’s kind of like his past life is coming back to haunt him.
  3. In turn, I felt like the GOC is used incorrectly in the first version. I feel like D.C al Fine is not directly involved, but more like the Serpent’s Hand is influencing her (like with mind control of sorts). She is allowing the GOC to help the Serpent’s Hand and Chaos Insurgency but I do plan on Orpheus killing or subduing her as a reference to the actual myth. I feel like I can change this to make the Serpent’s Hand member the one who loved Orpheus but D.C al Fine is controlled by that girl.
  4. Admittedly the UIU is a side character, kind of referencing the fact that the UIU is infamously lacking in resources to get involved. They are the first to investigate and the UIU are involved with Three Portlands, which is why I felt the need to include them in a way. Besides that they are kind of pushed to the side after Orpheus begins trying to resurrect Eurydice.
  5. The GOC, Serpent’s Hand, and Chaos Insurgency fully agree on giving reality benders civil rights, that is the common goal with the three groups. But how this goal is effective with each group is what makes this a shaky alliance. The Serpent’s Hand is the only group that is committed to this cause, so they are the puppet masters of sorts. The Chao’s Insurgency are willing to utilize reality benders, so by giving them civil rights they are employees rather than tools. This is why the Serpent’s Hand is allying with the Chaos Insurgency. The GOC is a little out of place, but like explained on #3 the Serpent’s Hand can have mild control over D.C al Fine, making the GOC the military body of the alliance. I also feel like I can expand upon this in that while the GOC’s main goal is the destruction of anomalies, the Secret Council of 108 might be convinced to allow reality benders to be people.

These in response to each point you gave. I intend to edit the thread to make it more comprehensive but this is more of a list for me.
Thank you very much for the critique.

item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

After an anomalous event, the UIU begin a file after finding an anomalous harp.

I'm assuming the harp is in some way related to the event?

find that the GOC, Serpent’s Hand (SH), and Chaos Insurgency (CI) are starting a war with hundreds of civilian casualties.

Why are they starting a war with a lot of civilian casualties? Why are the TMI/Foundation not paying enough attention to notice this already? How does this war actually like, tie into the narrative here?

Like the war seems kinda important to the SCP but also kinda…background-y? It's weird.

the GOC Leader (who is anomalous) loved Orpheus

The idea of the GOC having like, one leader who can just, unilaterally decide to do things feels kinda jarring? Like, arguably D.C. al Fine is the leader but she has to answer to the UN and a secret council of 108 so like…it feels weird that she can just do all this for personal reasons without being fired?

After finding the UIU helping Orpheus, all 4 of them go to Three Portlands to find Eurydice, with Three Portlands being in civil unrest as a war for civil rights occurs.

…why do the UIU team up here?

They all allied after realizing that killing an O5 member would be a powerful enough message.

I don't understand why they allied here? The GOC have very different aims to the SH/CI here; and it's not even clear why the CI/SH are aligned cos they also have generally different aims.

I think, at the end of the day, my issue with this is that there's a lot of moving parts and stuff going on here and it feels…bloated? Like, you have 6 different GoIs1 involved in this story and big plot twists relating to like two different leaders of the GoIs and there's this whole thing about them being greek folk but it doesn't particularly seem to matter really beyond the reference to the classical myth. It's hard to put my finger on what this feels like it's missing exactly but I think it's a sense of…coherence? I don't really follow why these events are occurring or what's motivating folk here; so it just feels very arbitrary in a way that doesn't really jive with me.

This being a SCP article feels like a huge mistake too; like, it feels like you could tell a much tighter story if you didn't have to worry about e.g. clinical tone or how the Foundation got certain logs, and instead could just…prose it up, y'know? Show the story unfolding from the PoV of the various GoIs involved, really let us get into the head of Orpheus and stuff and understand why they're so driven and all that.

Footnotes
1. Well, technically the foundation isn't a goi but i'm gonna keep using that for shortness

item.title: Greenlight - To Go Hell and Back
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Love, Drama/Emotional, Action, Mystery (Mild)

Page Layout:

  • This is a longer article.
  • Short containment procedure and description, as the anomalies are neutralized.
  • The idea of the story is that the addendums tell the story. Kind of like SCP-1730.
  • Serpent’s Hand = SH | The Gate Guardian = GG
  • I will definitely be missing certain aspects of the story, based on the 400 word limit.
  • If you wish to understand some aspects of this thread, please look through the post below titled “Explaining My Plot Holes” to understand the tone of my concept.
Tab For Space
My Concept/Idea

Elevator Pitch:

How far will someone go for love?
Because Orpheus was the only one willing To Go Hell And Back for his beloved…

Central Narrative:
The anomaly is a deceased female that is being preserved using advanced cryogenics. She is anomalously beautiful, with every man viewing her differently but all agreeing that she is extremely beautiful. She also had the ability to change the state of matter around her hands, wearing black gloves to control her ability. She is O5-2, who was killed by the SH while secretly getting married with her husband.

The Foundation investigates her death and after the events described below, an event log was created.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Essentially O5-2, Eurydice, secretly dated an anomalous musician named Orpheus, a former member of the SH. To prevent the Council from knowing of her affair, Eurydice barely uses Foundation resources to prevent suspicions. Not to mention, Eurydice hides her troops to keep a shellshocked Orpheus as comfortable as possible. The SH, wanting to tie up loose ends, planned to kill Orpheus and use Eurydice as a bargaining chip to get certain anomalies from the Foundation. They launch a multi-pronged assault, with Eurydice sacrificing herself to save Orpheus and allowing him to escape.

Rather than fighting the SH, he plans on resurrecting Eurydice. He uses his harp to disguise himself and enter Site-19 to ask SCP-343 “how to resurrect Eurydice.” SCP-343 tells him that “it requires the convincing of the Arch-Drudgeon,” something SCP-343 doesn’t want to get involved with. After this discussion, the Foundation are able to follow Orpheus. He establishes a plan to convince JALAKARA in resurrecting Eurydice, entering The Wanderer’s Library to find “The Song of Minor.” He encounters the SH and subdues Cerberus to obtain the song. Orpheus begins traveling to Site 0.

He arrives to Site 0 and uses a verse to please the GG, with the GG leading Orpheus through the gate and directly to JALAKARA’s doorstep. JALAKARA is obviously pissed, but Orpheus sings the song and is given a chance to resurrect Eurydice. He does his famous trial and fails, dragging Eurydice’s dead body out of the gate. He is attacked by the SH, in which he allows himself to be ripped apart by the group and dies to the wounds.

Additional Notes:
The Foundation obtains the body dragged out by Orpheus, trying everything to resurrect the O5-2.
